Marketers often assume viewers skip every ad they see. Reality tells a different story: when an ad feels relevant, 69% of consumers say they’re happy to watch it through. That shift in attitude, combined with streaming’s dominance, makes local Connected TV advertising one of the most efficient channels available today.


Yet efficiency only happens when TV advertising costs stay in check. Local CTV campaigns routinely deliver significant ROAS for performance-focused brands, but only when marketers understand the variables that drive spend. Let’s take a look at **local TV advertising costs** , updated for today’s programmatic landscape.


## How Much Does a Local TV Commercial Cost to Air?


Airing a local TV commercial typically costs between **$200 and $50,000+ for a 30-second spot and $300 to $100,000+ for a 60-second spot** , with prices varying significantly by market size and time slot. In smaller markets, 30-second spots range from $200 to $1,500 while 60-second spots run from $300 to $3,000; in top-10 Media Markets, those figures jump to $5,000–$50,000+ for 30 seconds and $7,500–$100,000+ for 60 seconds.


Local TV airtime generally averages a **CPM of $15 to $35, with $20–$25** being the most commonly cited benchmark. Of course, this depends heavily on the platform you’re using, as CPMs vary widely between traditional cable TV advertising deals (that use much broader audience targeting) and streaming TV advertising platforms (that use more advanced and granular targeting).

## How Much Does a Local TV Commercial Cost to Produce?


Producing a local TV commercial typically costs between **$1,500 and $15,000 for a 30-second spot and $2,500 to $50,000 for a 60-second spot** when working with local production teams. Brands can drive those numbers even lower—down to $0–$5,000 for a 30-second ad—by using DIY approaches or AI-powered tools.


With that said, exact budgets vary depending on script complexity, filming, editing, talent, and post-production needs.


## 10 Factors That Influence Local TV Advertising Costs


So, what goes into all of those costs? Quite a bit, actually. Here are the main cost drivers to consider when deciding whether or not local TV advertising is for you.


### **1. Target Audience**


Audience size and specificity remain the biggest drivers of local TV advertising costs. The broader the reach, the higher the price. Precision targeting on CTV platforms reduces wasted impressions by up to 90% by focusing on high-intent households through machine learning and first-party data.


### 2. **Geographic Reach**


The geographic scope of your campaign significantly affects local TV ad costs. CTV platforms enable hyper-local geotargeting down to specific zip codes, cities, or even a custom radius around your store, delivering far greater efficiency than buying an entire Media Market on linear TV.


### 3. **Creative Production Costs**


High-quality video creative is essential, but[video production](https://quickframe.com/blog/video-production-process/) expenses—from scripting and filming to editing and post-production—can add up quickly.


### 4. **Ad Placement Types**


CTV offers multiple placement options beyond traditional broadcast spots, from pre-roll to shoppable ads and interactive overlays. These formats often command premium CPMs but drive significantly higher conversion rates.


### 5. **Time Slots and Channel Selection**


CTV provides greater flexibility in time slots and content targeting than linear TV’s rigid prime-time model. You can schedule ads during optimal viewing windows and align them with specific genres, often lowering costs while boosting relevance and engagement.


### 6. **Duration and Frequency of Ads**


Shorter 15-second ads typically cost 50-80% less than 30-second spots. Higher frequency improves recall and brand awareness but burns through budget faster, so striking the right balance is key to cost efficiency.


### 7. **Seasonal Demand Spikes**


Seasonal demand spikes during holidays, election years, major sporting events, and Q4 retail periods can dramatically drive up local TV advertising costs due to heightened competition for inventory.


### 8. **Competitive Bidding and Auction Dynamics**


Most CTV inventory is sold through real-time auctions where you set budgets and bids. Smart platforms adjust bids dynamically based on conversion probability, helping you stay competitive without overpaying.


### 9. **Duration of Advertising Campaign**


Longer campaigns generally achieve lower CPMs than multiple short flights with the same total budget. Extended runs also allow for better optimization and sustained audience presence.


### **10. CTV Platform Selection**


Choosing the right platform is critical, as native streamer options often limit reach, targeting, and add extra fees for analytics. A unified Performance TV solution provides premium inventory, advanced tools, and full support at no additional cost.


## How to Budget for Local TV Ads


Effective budgeting for local TV ads starts with focusing on measurable performance rather than just chasing the lowest rates. Here are a few timeless best practices to follow.


### Set Clear Performance Goals Upfront


Clearly defining your campaign objectives and key performance metrics prevents overspending on tactics that don’t drive results. This focused approach ensures every dollar is allocated toward the channels, time slots, and creative most likely to deliver measurable outcomes.


### Prioritize Precision Audience Targeting


Narrowing your reach to high-intent households and specific geographic areas dramatically reduces wasted impressions. Hyper-local and data-driven targeting lets you connect with the right viewers without paying for broad, untargeted Media Market coverage.


### Schedule During Off-Peak and Shoulder Time Slots


Running ads outside expensive prime-time windows can cut airtime costs significantly while still reaching engaged audiences. Strategic timing paired with relevant content programming delivers better engagement at a fraction of peak rates.


### Leverage Efficient Creative Production


Using AI-powered tools and streamlined workflows keeps creative costs low without sacrificing quality. Brands can quickly produce multiple high-performing variations, freeing up more budget for media spend.


### Commit to Longer Campaign Durations


Longer campaigns typically secure lower CPMs and allow more time for real-time optimization. This extended approach improves overall efficiency compared to multiple short, high-intensity flights with the same total budget.


## Is Local TV Advertising Worth the Investment?


Traditional cable TV advertising relies on broad Media Market buys and fixed linear schedules, which forces advertisers to pay for large, untargeted audiences. In contrast, Connected TV advertising uses programmatic buying on streaming services, delivering precise household-level targeting and flexible scheduling within the same local market.


This precision makes CTV superior for local TV advertising because it dramatically reduces wasted impressions and enables real-time optimization based on actual performance data. As a result, local marketers achieve stronger efficiency, measurable outcomes, and better return on every advertising dollar compared to traditional cable.
